history.summary: The Sun Temple stands on a hill at Edalhatu village near Bundu, about 40 km southeast of Ranchi on the Ranchi-Tata highway (NH-43) — the CSV town 'Ranchi' has been corrected to Bundu. It was built by the Sanskriti Vihar Charitable Trust under Shri Sita Ram Maroo (Managing Director of the Ranchi Express Group): the foundation stone was laid by Swami Shri Vasudevanand Saraswati on 24 October 1991 and the prana pratishtha was performed by Swami Shri Vamdev Ji Maharaj on 10 July 1994. The temple is designed as a huge chariot with eighteen wheels and seven horses, inspired by the Konark Sun Temple in Odisha, and enshrines a 2.5-foot Surya idol; shrines for Shiva, Parvati, Ganesha and Hanuman stand in the same complex, with a sacred pond for Chhath rituals and a dharamshala for pilgrims.

name: Sun Temple, Ranchi
town_description: Bundu is a small town in Ranchi district, Jharkhand, on the Ranchi-Tata highway (NH-43) about 40 km southeast of Ranchi. It lies among the forested hills of the Chota Nagpur Plateau and is best known for its chariot-shaped Sun Temple. The surrounding countryside of villages, lakes and waterfalls draws pilgrims and day-trippers from Ranchi.
